content.value_statement: Teams often need repeatable agent workflows but lack a clear skill structure. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through planning, scaffolding, editing, packaging, and iteration.
actual_capabilities: Explains when to create or update an AI skill.
Defines the expected SKILL.md structure and metadata.
Guides planning for scripts, references, and assets.
Provides an initialization script for standard skill folders.
Provides a packaging script that validates and zips a skill.
Documents progressive disclosure and iteration practices.
limitations: Generated templates require manual completion before use.
The packaging script validates structure, not task quality.
It does not publish skills to any remote marketplace.
Local scripts should be reviewed before execution.

use_cases.title: Build a New Agent Skill
use_cases.description: Plan a new skill, create the folder structure, and draft the required SKILL.md instructions.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Workflows
use_cases.description: Convert repeated internal processes into reusable skill instructions, scripts, references, and assets.

use_cases.title: Prepare Skills for Sharing
use_cases.description: Validate skill metadata, remove placeholders, and package the folder into a distributable archive.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Simple Skill
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a first skill.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me plan a skill for a repeated task. Ask for the examples you need, then propose the skill name, purpose, triggers, and basic workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Create the Skill Structure
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a new skill for my workflow. Use a clear skill name, include SKILL.md, and add only the resource folders that the workflow needs.

prompt_templates.title: Improve an Existing Skill
prompt_templates.scenario: Refine a skill that already exists.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this existing skill and improve its trigger description, workflow steps, bundled resources, and validation readiness.

prompt_templates.title: Package and Validate a Skill
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare this skill for distribution. Check for incomplete placeholders, validate metadata, review bundled resources, and package the skill when it is ready.

output_examples.input: I need a skill that helps agents create release notes from pull requests.
output_examples.output: A proposed release-notes skill plan with trigger guidance, a concise workflow, recommended references, and validation steps.

output_examples.input: Review my existing support-triage skill before I share it.
output_examples.output: A quality review covering metadata clarity, workflow completeness, unnecessary files, placeholder cleanup, and packaging readiness.

output_examples.input: Package this finished skill for distribution.
output_examples.output: A validation summary and a local archive created after the skill passes required structure checks.

best_practices: Keep SKILL.md focused on essential workflow guidance.
Move detailed schemas or long references into separate files.
Validate scripts and packaging before sharing a skill.
anti_patterns: Do not include unrelated documentation files in the skill folder.
Do not leave TODO placeholders in published skills.
Do not duplicate the same instructions across SKILL.md and references.

faq.question: What does this skill help create?
faq.answer: It helps create and update AI skills with structured instructions, optional resources, validation, and packaging.

faq.question: Does it work with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance is useful for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code skill workflows.

faq.question: Does it generate a complete finished skill automatically?
faq.answer: No. It creates structure and guidance, but the author must fill in domain-specific content.

faq.question: Can it include scripts and reference files?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains when scripts, references, and assets are useful for repeatable agent tasks.

faq.question: Does it publish skills online?
faq.answer: No. It packages skills locally and does not upload them to any service.

faq.question: What should I check before sharing a skill?
faq.answer: Check metadata, remove placeholders, test scripts, validate structure, and confirm that bundled files are necessary.
